name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Tuesday 18 February 1975

clue.text: A Monsieur Fish has a gown for Her Excellency

blocks.note: taken as written
M. is the abbreviation for Monsieur
the bass is a sea fish
taken as written
a gown is a long dress

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with a fishy name presents a gown to a lady of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Fish makes it look like Monsieur's surname, but it is just the fish, a bass.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's wife was formally styled Her Excellency, the courtesy title shared with her husband.

clue.text: Blind fury of a sport upset about nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom
about means around, so the word wraps itself around what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sporting loss sets off a blind rage over nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton's Lycidas calls the Fate who cuts the thread of life 'the blind Fury with th'abhorred shears', so the definition is a literary quotation, not plain anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropos, the Fate who cuts life's thread, is the blind Fury of Milton's poem, a classical allusion.

clue.text: Better avoid - those with'. Welsh tendencies

definitions.text: Better avoid - those with'. Welsh tendencies

blocks.note: surface reading: it would be wiser to keep away from people inclined to Welshness
setter's reading: a better is a gambler, and to welsh is to fail to pay out on a bet

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like 'it is better to', but it is one who bets; 'welsh' is not the nationality but the verb for dodging a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookies take bets, and a punter should shun any who might welsh, refusing to pay winnings owed.

clue.text: -Tom alas in trouble in Brittany

indicators.note: letters in trouble are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, all nine letters

explanation.surface: Poor Tom has got himself into difficulty while visiting north-western France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' after 'alas' looks like part of 'in trouble', but its letters are needed in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is a walled port town on the north coast of Brittany, so it is a place found there.

clue.text: A submarine-spotter like Richard?

blocks.note: like means as, and Dick is the familiar form of Richard

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man called Richard is the sort to watch for submarines.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a pun: said aloud, the device's name runs together 'as Dick'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic was the British sonar system used by warships to detect submerged submarines by echoes.

clue.text: Playful Edmond gets round Stanley in a way '

indicators.note: something set in another thing sits inside it, so the ring and the name go within the way

blocks.note: Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
a round shape is the letter O
Stan is the short form of Stanley

explanation.surface: A frolicsome Edmond travels a road around a man named Stanley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playful' looks like a mood, but it means given to writing plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmond Rostand was the French dramatist who wrote Cyrano de Bergerac, so he is a playwright named Edmond.

clue.text: But these cats have no connexion with each other

definitions.text: But these cats have no connexion with each other

blocks.note: surface reading: some unrelated felines that happen to share nothing
setter's reading: the famous twins of this name were joined, but the cats of the same name are not

explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'But' points to the contrast with conjoined twins, who share the same name as this breed of cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Siamese is a breed of cat from Thailand and also the old term for conjoined twins, hence the contrast.

clue.text: Premier Chippendale

blocks.note: first meaning: a prime minister, who forms the government's cabinet
second meaning: Thomas Chippendale, the great English furniture craftsman

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a brand of top-quality furniture; the first word is a head of government, who literally makes a cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinetmaker is a craftsman of fine furniture, as Chippendale was, and a prime minister picks a ministerial team called a cabinet.

clue.text: A monk states his seniority deductively

blocks.note: taken as written
a prior is a monk who ranks just below the abbot
the monk speaking of himself uses the first person

explanation.surface: A monastic brother announces where he stands in the pecking order by careful reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as the monk's statement 'A prior, I': he declares he is a prior, which is his seniority.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning a priori works from principles to consequences, which is reasoning by deduction rather than from experience.

clue.text: The female side has 501 employees

blocks.note: in Roman numerals D is 500 and I is 1
a firm's employees are its staff

explanation.surface: A company boasts that its women's division employs exactly 501 people.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the mother's side, from the spinning staff long associated with women's work.

clue.text: A little square, the condition of the Press

blocks.note: a fourth is a quarter, a small square cut from a larger square
estate in its old sense of state or condition

explanation.surface: A small town square describes the state the newspapers are in.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is only loosely clued: a quarter of a square is itself a smaller square, so 'a little square' stands for a fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalism is called the fourth estate, ranked after the clergy, nobility and commons as a power in the realm.

clue.text: Impression caused >by public relations in one money-making concern

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the relations go within the concern

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
PR is the usual abbreviation for public relations
the mint is where coins are made, literally making money

explanation.surface: A firm's reputation was shaped by its publicity people working inside one profitable business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money-making concern' looks like any profitable business, but here it is the place that literally makes coins.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprint is a mark pressed into a surface, so it is an impression in the physical sense.

clue.text: A French vine-grower's home too

blocks.note: surface reading: the house of someone who grows grapes in France
setter's reading: the wine estates of Bordeaux are each named after the grand house that stands on them

explanation.walkthrough: The final 'too' is not explained by this reading and may be a scanning error in this copy; the rest is a straight description of a Bordeaux wine estate's house.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux wine estates are known by the name of their country house, so a grower's residence there is a chateau.

clue.text: Comforts some judge as essential

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters lifted from across them

blocks.note: the run spans the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A judge decides which comforts are necessities.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone is to relieve their pain or worry, which is a synonym of comfort as a verb.

clue.text: Change' of - motion may do Bill some good

blocks.note: first meaning: an alteration proposed to a motion in a debate
second meaning: a correction that improves a parliamentary bill

explanation.surface: A change of movement, perhaps a new exercise, might help a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B makes Bill look like a person who needs a change of motion; it is a draft law, which is improved by amending it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a formal change made to a motion or a bill, and the word also means an improvement.

clue.text: He turns up without Dr Ellis to improve appearances

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that turns up is read from the bottom upward
without in its old sense of outside, so the word stands around the doctor

blocks.note: taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man shows up without his physician, Dr Ellis, to make a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, as in old hymns, not lacking; Dr Ellis looks like one person but splits into a degree and a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish is to decorate or adorn so that something looks better, a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: For which Tommy needed a safety-pin

definitions.text: For which Tommy needed a safety-pin

blocks.clueFragment: For which Tommy needed a safety-pin
blocks.note: surface reading: a little boy needing a safety pin for his nappy or torn trousers
setter's reading: the soldier's hand grenade, which is kept safe by a pin pulled before throwing

explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the nickname for a British private soldier; the Mills grenade was the standard British hand grenade of both World Wars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mills bomb was a British hand grenade armed by pulling out its safety pin, so a soldier needed one.

clue.text: Loyal Scots' include legislation concerning milk

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: leal is the Scottish word for loyal
an Act is a piece of legislation passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Faithful Scotsmen push for a law to regulate the dairy trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacteal means relating to or resembling milk, from the Latin word for milk, so it is the adjective required.

clue.text: Most hasty, they say

blocks.note: surface reading: whoever is in the greatest hurry
setter's reading: the proverb 'least said

explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' points to a saying; the answer is the word from 'least said, soonest mended', meaning earliest or quickest.
explanation.definitionFit: Soonest means earliest or quickest, the superlative of soon, close to the idea of greatest haste.

clue.text: Decoration worn by man of honour in the French way

indicators.note: something placed in another thing sits inside it, so the honour goes inside the way

blocks.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
rue is French for street, a way

explanation.surface: A medal pinned on a gentleman of honour, worn in the French style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoration worn by man of honour' reads as a medal; the definition is just 'Decoration', a dressmaker's trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a pleated or gathered frill of fabric used as trimming on a garment, an ornamental addition.

clue.text: He fixes both ends of the tackle in the river

indicators.note: both ends of a word are its first and last letters, keeping only the outside pair
something put in another thing sits inside it, so the pair goes within the river

blocks.note: the first and last letters of tackle
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler secures each end of his fishing gear while standing in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Tackle and river conjure fishing; the answer is a metalworker who joins plates with rivets.
explanation.definitionFit: A riveter is a worker who fastens metal parts together with rivets, so he is a man who fixes things.

clue.text: How rust may penetrate some distance into the heart of the fruit

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up inside it, so the distance sits within the heart

blocks.note: a rod is an old unit of length, five and a half yards
the core is the central part of an apple or pear

explanation.surface: Rust eats its way a little distance into the middle of an apple.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to eat away gradually by chemical action, which is exactly how rust attacks iron.

clue.text: No thrill on the menu at the start of play

blocks.note: a kick is a thrill, as in getting a kick out of something
with 'on the menu': a dish that is no longer on the menu is off
completes the phrase that No begins, describing a dish that has run out

explanation.surface: A dull meal disappoints a diner just before the show starts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a restaurant a dish that has run out is 'off'; so a thrill that is no longer on the menu is a kick that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: The kick-off starts a football match, so it is the opening moment of play.

clue.text: Criminal paling

blocks.note: first meaning: a crook who receives and sells stolen goods
second meaning: a barrier made of pointed wooden stakes

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an outlaw turning pale; 'paling' is the noun for a picket fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is slang for a receiver of stolen property and is also a barrier of posts such as a paling.

clue.text: Youngster in form may one day end up in jug

definitions.text: Youngster in form may one day end up in jug

blocks.clueFragment: Youngster in form may one day end up in jug
blocks.note: surface reading: a schoolboy in a school form who may one day land in prison, 'jug'
setter's reading: a young hare lying in its form, its nest, which may end up cooked as jugged hare

explanation.walkthrough: A hare's resting hollow is called its form, and jugged hare is hare stewed in a covered jug; 'jug' is also slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, the young animal that lies in a form and may be jugged.

clue.text: This alma mater's an unusually dear one

indicators.note: something done unusually is done out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, all seven letters

explanation.surface: A graduate speaks fondly of their old school as an exceptionally beloved place.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a girls' boarding school on the Sussex coast near Brighton, one of England's best known.
explanation.definitionFit: An alma mater is the school one attended, and Roedean is a famous English school, an example of one.

clue.text: In the race King of France comes in with Church Music

indicators.note: the king arrives inside the race, so he is placed within it

blocks.note: taken as written
the TT, the Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race
roi is French for king

explanation.surface: A French monarch joins a race accompanied by sacred music.
explanation.definitionFit: The introit is the psalm or anthem sung as the priest enters at the start of Mass, a piece of liturgical music.

clue.text: You can safely put your shirt on it

definitions.text: You can safely put your shirt on it

blocks.clueFragment: You can safely put your shirt on it
blocks.note: surface reading: a racing certainty, worth betting everything you own on
setter's reading: a frame on which a washed shirt is literally hung to dry

explanation.walkthrough: To put your shirt on a horse is to bet everything on it; this kind of horse is a wooden airer for laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse is a folding frame for drying or airing laundry, so shirts are put on it without risk.
